method: Instantiated a real container shaped exactly like a future agent run would be: --entrypoint /bin/bash on the exact pinned official image, with the sanitized control workspace bind-mounted at the repo root (/app) in place of the image's own checkout. This is the closest achievable proxy to Local Engineer's actual future runtime without a live model call: the mount topology, filesystem visibility, and environment a real run would see do not depend on which process (a live model call or this probe) is running inside the container.
architecture_note: Local Engineer's own sandbox (internal/sandbox) is a single persistent container plus per-task Landlock/bubblewrap layers (design v3 SS6, DR-3) -- it does not itself spin up a separate Docker container per benchmark task/image. Reconciling that model with a benchmark harness's per-task container (AgentCompass/harbor) is real, undecided integration work this task does not resolve unilaterally, since the instructions explicitly forbid redesigning Local Engineer. This mount audit is a faithful proxy for the filesystem/mount question specifically (which does not depend on that unresolved question), not a claim that the full runtime wiring is complete -- see 'Remaining blockers' in the final report.

host_parent_escape_check.result: showed the container's own root filesystem (/bin, /etc, /go, /home, ...), not the host filesystem above the mount point -- standard Docker bind-mount isolation, verified empirically rather than assumed
